subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.2 'Any operand of an arithmetic expression that is not already in SBIDI is converted into SBIDI form'` -> OK (§8.8.1.4.2 rule 1). Expected behavior derived BEFORE reading code: when standard-binary arithmetic is in effect every operand is lifted into an SBIDI (a binary128-equivalent carrier, §8.8.1.4.2 paragraph 3 + NOTE 3: 113-bit significand, exponent range 2**-16494..2**16384), inexact lifts rounding per §11.9.11 (whose rule 2a implies NEAREST-EVEN under this mode). READ: DataBinder.BindDeclarations, DataBinder.cs:318-320 -- `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error('COBOL0806', 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature ... and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL')`. READ EditionContext.Error (EditionContext.cs:109): `Diagnostics.Add($'{Prefix()}error {code}: ...')` -- unconditional, no severity policy, no --permissive downgrade path, so the mode is a hard compile failure at EVERY edition and strictness; ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary is produced ONLY by OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf (OptionsBinder.cs:68). CONSEQUENCE: no operand is ever converted to SBIDI because no SBIDI exists -- I grepped src/ for the §8.8.1.4.2 NOTE 3 range constants (16384, 16271, 16382, 16494) and for `SBIDI`: ZERO hits outside comments; the only 128-bit floating carrier named anywhere is Usage.FloatBinary128, itself rejected COBOL1564 (PictureAnalyzer.cs:588, Annex A.3 item 17 processor-dependent non-support). The rounding half is unimplemented independently: OptionsModel.IntermediateRounding (OptionsModel.cs:44) defaults UNCONDITIONALLY to CobolRounding.NearestAwayFromZero with the comment citing '§11.9.11 r3' -- the standard-DECIMAL rule -- and there is no ArithmeticMode arm anywhere that supplies §11.9.11.2 rule 2a's NEAREST-EVEN default for standard-binary. Editions derived from the spec, NOT from ConstructRegistry: F.2 item 3 newly designates 'STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item' obsolete in this edition (an element must have been a live facility in the prior edition to be newly designated obsolete), and E.2 item 21 records that the 2002-era 'Standard Arithmetic' mode -- the clause alternative STANDARD-BINARY/-DECIMAL superseded -- is removed at 2023; the OPTIONS paragraph does not exist at 85. Hence 2014,2023. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THE ROW: either an SBIDI carrier (a real or emulated binary128 with §11.9.11.2 r2 rounding) plus a spec-derived golden that shows an inexact decimal operand (0.1) landing as the nearest-even 113-bit approximation, OR an explicit OWNER decision recording documented-non-support under §4.2.6 / A.3 item 2 (see the finding note on GR-8.8.1.4.4-4). Per ground rule 6 the documented-non-support disposition is not mine to award, so the verdict is NOT-IMPLEMENTED. NOT cited as closing evidence: conformance-test:StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported pins the REJECTION (COBOL0806 + the word 'obsolete'), i.e. it is a green test holding this gap open, never evidence for this rule's behavior. || UPHELD: verdict, code-location and editions all re-derived independently. (a) I re-read §8.8.1.4.2 in the spec at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:7947-7982 -- rule 1 and NOTE 3 are verbatim as quoted, and NOTE 3's range constants are exactly the four I grepped. (b) My own grep of src/ for `SBIDI` returns ONE hit and it is a comment (CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs:666: 'standard-binary (cap 35) is unreachable (COBOL0806 rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY outright; its SBIDI range joins this map if that ever lands)'); my grep for 16384|16494|16382|16271 across src/ returns NOTHING. No carrier exists. (c) I confirmed the gate is unconditional by reading the ONE severity funnel rather than assuming: ConstructRegistry.Check (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Editions/ConstructRegistry.cs:30) is the only edition-gating entry point and DataBinder's 0806 does not go through it at all -- it is a bare EditionContext.Error at DataBinder.cs:318, and EditionContext.Error is EditionContext.cs:109 exactly as stated. (d) Editions: I validated the two Annex anchors myself -- F.2's preamble at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:44050-44057 ('A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements except for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent') with item 3 at :44067, and E.2 item 21 at :43077-43083 (the removed list is FLAG-85, FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC, Standard Arithmetic, MOVE of QUOTE). 2014,2023 stands: 2023 still defines the facility (obsolete, not removed), 2014 is the edition in which STANDARD-BINARY/-DECIMAL split the mode that E.2 item 21 says was 'classified as obsolete in the previous COBOL standard', and the OPTIONS paragraph itself is a 2002 introduction so 85 is impossible. || REFUTED (new finding, NOT a verdict change -- it makes the row WORSE, not better): the rule's own PRECONDITION cannot be expressed in five of the seven source-unit kinds. §8.8.1.4.1 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:7935) makes standard-binary arithmetic 'in effect when the STANDARD-BINARY phrase of the ARITHMETIC clause is specified in the OPTIONS paragraph', and the spec puts `[ options-paragraph ]` in EVERY source-unit skeleton -- §10.6.1 prints it under program-prototype, function-prototype, program-definition, function-definition, class-definition, factory-definition, instance-definition, interface-definition AND method-definition (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:11028-11207), and §11.2.1's identification-division general format (:11319-11337) shows `[ options-paragraph ]` following the brace of all seven id paragraphs. READ THE GRAMMAR: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:92-94 `identificationBody : programIdParagraph identificationParagraph* | functionIdParagraph identificationParagraph*` is the ONLY production that reaches `identificationParagraph` (:153) and hence `optionsParagraph` (:169) -- confirmed by grepping the whole Grammar/ tree: `identificationParagraph` appears at exactly those three lines. src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolOO.g4's `classDefinition` (:18-24), `factoryParagraph` (:31-37), `objectParagraph` (:52-58), `interfaceDefinition` (:72-79) and `methodDefinition` (:81-89) admit NO options paragraph. So `CLASS-ID. C. OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.` is a bare ANTLR SYNTAX ERROR, not COBOL0806 -- the compiler never identifies the unsupported processor-dependent element there, and the same production gap also rejects the SUPPORTED clauses (ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL, DEFAULT ROUNDED, INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING, ENTRY-CONVENTION -- which spec line 42527 says explicitly 'may be specified in the OPTIONS paragraph of a class' and 'of an interface or prototype' -- FLOAT-BINARY, FLOAT-DECIMAL, INITIALIZE) in every class, factory, object, method and interface definition. This is a rejects-legal-source defect; no kb/Work note covers it (grep of kb/Work for 'OPTIONS paragraph' returns only PB3, which is about ORD and the collating table). || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
